title: Polynomial-time graph isomorphism
decision_reason: Ren–Li 2024 primary abstract claims a matching cubic-time algorithm. Its full proof and independent adjudication were not obtained. A 2026 specialist survey still treats the general problem as open. Keep outside accepted count.

problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: All n; no degree, genus or width restriction
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: One deterministic algorithm with universal polynomial bound for every graph pair
problem_fingerprint.normalization: Standard bit-time on explicit graph input
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Existence of a vertex bijection preserving adjacency in both directions
problem_fingerprint.requested_conclusion: Decide graph isomorphism in deterministic polynomial time
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: Unconditional uniform Turing model; not restricted graph classes or heuristic average-case performance

statement_source_and_scope_match: N26 §1 and §2.1 give the general decision question and unresolved polynomial bound; RL24 indexed primary abstract appears to claim that same scope.
proposed_statement_text: Is there a deterministic Turing algorithm and constants K,c such that, for every pair of simple undirected n-vertex graphs G,H given by adjacency matrices, the algorithm decides in at most K n^c steps whether a bijection phi:V(G)->V(H) preserves adjacency in both directions?
applied_significance: Graph identity under relabeling underlies comparison and indexing of relational structures; N26 traces the computational problem to chemical information systems.
